about.title: Santa Monica Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Monica packs a lot of traffic into a small footprint. Beach visitors funnel down Lincoln Boulevard, commuters pour off the I-10 where the Santa Monica Freeway ends, and Pacific Coast Highway carries a steady stream north out of town. In 2025, the city recorded 445 injury collisions, with 572 people injured and 5 lives lost. Public records show reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m., when the workweek and the weekend crowd overlap. If you were hurt in one of those collisions, the days that follow can feel disorienting: medical appointments, calls from an adjuster you did not choose, and a car you may not be able to drive. We handle car accident claims in Los Angeles County on a contingency basis. Tell us what happened, and our team will review your case at no cost. You decide whether to move forward; there is no charge for the consultation, and no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Monica Drivers Choose Us

items.title: The clock is already running
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident injury claims, but if a city, county, or state vehicle or road condition was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. Getting started early protects those deadlines.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly to blame; your share of responsibility simply reduces the amount. We can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: Evidence and recorded statements matter
items.desc: Dashcam footage, 4th Street business cameras, and witness contacts fade fast, and the other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement before you have counsel. Our team helps you preserve what matters and speaks on your behalf.

items.question: My crash happened on Pacific Coast Highway. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. PCH is a state route, so if a road condition, signal, or public vehicle played a role, part of your claim may be against a government entity, and that generally requires a formal claim within six months rather than the usual two years. We can sort out who is potentially responsible and which deadlines apply before anything lapses.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to assign you more fault later under California's comparative fault system. You can simply tell them your attorney will be in touch.

items.question: How do you charge for your services?
items.answer: We work on contingency, which means our fee comes out of any recovery we obtain for you, and if there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee. Whether to hire us is entirely your choice.
